current_stage.name: D123: 1.5-go prerequisite implementation + rehearsal in progress (unattended window, Hidenori away ~10h)
current_stage.description: 1-go's live archive is stable and published (D122) -- no action needed there. A proposed shortcut (dubbed "1.4-go": patch 1-go's existing generation in place with the D116 merge-bug fix, national scale) was aborted BEFORE launch when a comparison analysis found it would trigger a D76-class collision (aggregation_tile.py's cleanup glob could delete up to 3,344 legitimate downsampling files under the old flat layout). The .done/.todo staging already prepared for that launch was fully reverted -- 1-go's 6,373 aggregation items are confirmed back to .done, untouched. Decision: use the current unattended window to properly prepare and rehearse the fuller "1.5-go" arrangement instead (new generation_id, namespace separation + lineage + filename cleanup, one national run covers everything needed before 2-go) -- the actual national-scale launch itself is deliberately deferred to Hidenori's return and explicit approval, not attempted during this window. Currently in progress, two agents working in parallel against slate: one implementing the 1.5-go prerequisites (done/todo manifest datatype-scoping, a generation_id path layer, TMPDIR/run_command hardening) and running a real chained rehearsal in an isolated pipelines-rehearsal/ environment; a second independently deriving a pre-launch safety checklist from this project's own incident history, so the real implementation gets graded against independently-derived criteria rather than its own self-report. This progress.json is being refreshed roughly every 15 minutes during the window specifically so resource load can be checked remotely.
